title: Cobalt Insurance POC — inference benchmark deep dive
content:
Executive summary:

This document summarizes the inference benchmarking work we ran for the Cobalt Insurance conversational claim assistant POC. Goal: quantify latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), sustainable throughput (reqs/sec), and per-unit token cost across realistic workload mixes and two candidate serving configurations (hosted H100 pool vs Dedicated A100 reserve). Tests focus on: response latency for short question-answer flows (avg user message length ~20 tokens, model output ~80 tokens), longer multi-turn claim summarization flows (user+context ~400 tokens, output ~600 tokens), and a streaming scenario for agent-like step-by-step guidance.

Key takeaways (high level):
- H100-hosted configuration (Redwood Hosted): best raw latency on short requests (p95 ~72 ms, p99 ~150 ms) with burst-friendly autoscaling; cost per 1M tokens ~= $42 with default batching settings.
- Dedicated A100 configuration (1x reserved A100s, medium batch tuning): higher tail latency under multi-tenant saturation (p95 ~180 ms) but lower steady-state token cost (~$32/1M tokens) for sustained predictable load.
- Quantized 4-bit model variant (int4) reduced token CPU/GPU time by ~28% and reduced cost estimates by ~20% with negligible quality regression on our eval prompts for summaries.
- KV/cache prefix reuse produced the largest latency and cost wins on repeat-context flows: median latency drop of 45% and token-cost drop of 35% when prefix cache hit rate ~60%.

Test matrix and environments:

Environments:
- Hosted-H100: Redwood hosted cluster, H100 (80GB) instances; autoscaling enabled; default routing.
- Dedicated-A100: Customer-dedicated pool (2x A100-80GB), pinned model version, fixed capacity.

Model variants tested:
- model-v1 (fp16 baseline) — reference.
- model-v1-quant4 (int4) — production candidate.
- model-v1-kvcache-enabled — same as v1 with persistent KV cache across turns.

Workload profiles (collected from Cobalt telemetry + synthetic extension):
- Attendant (short Q/A): 60% of traffic, user tokens: 15–30, output tokens: 40–120. Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms.
- Claim summarizer (long): 30% traffic, input 350–450 tokens, output 500–700 tokens. SLO: p95 < 1500ms.
- Guided step stream (streaming): 10% traffic, intermittent short outputs (20–60 tokens) per step; streaming latency per chunk matters.

Test harness / methodology:
- Synthetic replay of traces using Redwood load runner (open-sourced harness), preserving arrival patterns (Poisson tail bursts) and session affinity for cache hits.
- Each scenario run for 30 minutes to capture autoscaling effects; long-run validation for 4 hours at target qps where applicable.
- Metrics collected: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, model-inqueue times, GPU kernel time, failure/oom counts, and cost estimation from profiling traces (tokenized units * cost model).
- Runs repeated 3x; median aggregated.

Results (representative numbers):

1) Short Q/A (attendant) — 100 reqs/sec target sustained (60% of workload)
- Hosted-H100 / model-v1 / batch=dynamic:
  - p50: 38 ms, p95: 72 ms, p99: 150 ms
  - throughput: 110 req/s (sustainable), GPU util: 42%
  - errors: 0.04% (timeouts during storm bursts)
  - estimated token cost: $0.000042 per token -> ~$42 per 1M tokens

- Dedicated-A100 / model-v1 / batch=64:
  - p50: 72 ms, p95: 180 ms, p99: 360 ms
  - throughput: 95 req/s (sustainable), GPU util: 67%
  - errors: 0.2% (queue timeouts under bursts)
  - estimated token cost: ~$0.000032 per token -> ~$32 per 1M tokens

- Dedicated-A100 / model-v1-quant4 / batch=64:
  - p50: 58 ms, p95: 150 ms, p99: 270 ms
  - throughput: 125 req/s, GPU util: 58%
  - cost: ~$25/1M tokens (est.)

2) Long summarization — 10 reqs/sec target sustained (30% of workload)
- Hosted-H100 / model-v1 / batch=dynamic:
  - p50: 680 ms, p95: 1180 ms, p99: 1900 ms
  - throughput: 12 req/s (sustainable), GPU util: 55%
  - cost: ~$0.000045 per token -> ~$45/1M tokens

- Dedicated-A100 / model-v1 / batch=32:
  - p50: 810 ms, p95: 1520 ms, p99: 2600 ms
  - throughput: 10 req/s, GPU util: 73%
  - cost: ~$34/1M tokens

- Dedicated-A100 / model-v1-quant4 / kvcache-enabled:
  - p50: 410 ms, p95: 780 ms, p99: 1250 ms (cache hit rate ~62%)
  - throughput: 18 req/s (effective), GPU util: 49%
  - cost: ~$22/1M tokens (effective)

3) Streaming scenario (per-chunk latency matters)
- Hosted-H100 / model-v1 with streaming enabled:
  - median first-chunk latency: 28 ms, subsequent-chunk latencies: 8–12 ms
  - observed smoothness: high, small tail spikes during cold starts

- Dedicated-A100 / model-v1-quant4 with streaming enabled:
  - median first-chunk latency: 48 ms, subsequent: 18–24 ms
  - good throughput once warmed; higher cold-start tail for first request in a session.

Observations and analysis:

- Latency vs cost tradeoffs: Hosted H100 gives the best short-tail latency for low-latency interactive flows, at a higher $/token. Dedicated A100 amortizes cost better for steady high-volume but shows higher tail under bursty mixed workloads unless we overprovision or tune autoscaling/fallbacks.

- Quantization: model-v1-quant4 is large win for cost and throughput with minimal observed quality drop on our reference claim-summary prompts. We recommend a controlled QA pass for edge-case legal phrasing before full rollout.

- KV cache: for Cobalt, the claim flows have high prefix reuse (templates + claim fragments). Prefix caching yields order-of-magnitude savings for long responses: lower GPU time for attention recompute and shorter wall-clock latency. Plan to enable persistent per-session KV caching for sessions with predictable multi-turns.

- Streaming UX: Hosted environment has faster first-chunk tails; if Cobalt’s product requires sub-100ms first-chunk for agent flow, Hosted is preferable or Dedicated must use warmed worker pools.

Failure modes noted:
- OOMs when experimenting with batch sizes >96 on Dedicated A100 for long summaries; mitigation was lowering per-GPU batch and enabling dynamic batching at runtime.
- Queue timeouts when Dedicated pool saturated by synthetic burst; solution: burst capacity or circuit-breaker fallbacks to a cheaper compact model.

Recommendations (actionable):

Short-term (next 2–4 weeks):
- Pilot model-v1-quant4 on Dedicated pool for production-like sustained traffic (QA gating): run the legal/regulatory prompt sweep and human evaluation on ~500 summaries (owner: Sofia).
- Enable per-session persistent KV cache for claim summarizer flows; measure real-world cache hit and re-run cost projection (owner: Ravi).
- For interactive agent flows where p95 < 200ms matters, use Hosted-H100 routing for the first rollout; configure routing policy to fallback to Dedicated when cost threshold reached (owner: Maya).

Medium-term (1–3 months):
- Add an autoscaling policy allowing short (2–5 minute) burst capacity on Dedicated pools or cheap fallback instances to absorb storms. Evaluate cost delta.
- Implement adaptive batching that reduces batch size on low-latency flagged routes while keeping high batching on background summarizer jobs.

Operational runbook excerpts (for SE / SRE):
- If p95 on Dedicated exceeds 2x baseline for >10 minutes, enable manual spillover to Hosted route and notify SE on-call. Pager: #se-pocs.
- When moving to quant4, watch for low-frequency hallucination or missing tokens; have rollback to fp16 version via model pin within Console.

Appendix: commands and configs used (short snippets)
- load-runner command pattern:
  rd-bench run --config cobalt-attendant.yml --duration 1800 --concurrency 400 --env hosted-h100 --model model-v1

- cost calc (simple):
  token_count_total * cost_per_token_by_config -> normalized to 1M tokens

- notable linked artifacts:
  - Confluence POC overview (linked above) for business requirements and SLOs.
  - JIRA-4201 contains the test schedule and dataset.

Open questions for Cobalt product team:
- Acceptable p99 for long summaries? (currently running ~1.2–2.6s depending on config)
- Will legal/regulatory QA accept quant4 variant for production? Need signoff path.

Notes to self / rough todos (working doc style):
- Run 24h soak with quant4 + kvcache to capture any long-tail mem leaks (Liam to schedule).
- Collect human evals for the 50 edge-case claims we saw in July data (Sofia).
- Draft customer-facing slide deck summarizing this doc for kickoff with Cobalt sponsors (Maya).

End of report.
